text: dsh-har-triage（DSH 插件，CLI）：离线读取浏览器 HAR 文件，帮助定位失败或缓慢的网络请求。它在 DSH 中注册 har_triage 工具，也提供 har-triage 命令行入口；分析请求状态、耗时和计时阶段，并生成 HTML 与 JSON 报告。报告用端点别名和原始条目索引呈现证据，不包含 URL、请求头、查询值、正文或绝对时间。适合需要检查本地 HAR 并回查原始请求的开发者。代码未要求 API key 或外部服务。

dsh-har-triage analyzes local HAR files offline and reports failed or slow requests. Its DSH tool and CLI create HTML and JSON reports with endpoint aliases and original entry indexes, omitting URLs, headers, query values, bodies, and absolute timestamps. No API key or external service is required.
我想从浏览器导出的 HAR 里找出失败的请求。
有没有办法离线查看哪些网络请求特别慢？
Can I turn a local HAR capture into a report of failed and slow requests?
dsh-har-triage 的功能「离线 HAR 诊断」：通过 har_triage 工具提供 HAR 路径和新报告目录，或使用命令行入口。它汇总请求状态与耗时，并生成 HTML 和 JSON 报告供本地查看。

dsh-har-triage README · HAR Triage：Offline network evidence for DeepSeek Harness. Find failed and slow browser requests without handing the agent your URLs, cookies or response bodies.

浏览器网络排障插件：读取本地 HAR，生成可回查原始请求索引的离线诊断报告。默认不把网址、请求头、Cookie、参数值或正文带进报告和 AI 工具结果。

The screenshot uses the bundled synthetic scenario, not real browser traffic.

dsh-har-triage README · What it does：- Reads an existing HAR 1.2 capture; never records traffic, sends requests, or changes the capture.
- Groups requests into endpoint aliases, highlights HTTP 4xx/5xx, unavailable responses, slow requests and long waiting phases.
- Produces a self-contained HTML report: signals → request row → measured timing phases. Filters, pagination and source locators work offline.
- Returns at most 20 evidence entries to the agent, with a count of omitted evidence. The full numeric projection stays in the local JSON/HTML files.

dsh-har-triage README · What it does：Request #43 corresponds to `log.entries[42]` in your original HAR. Endpoint aliases deliberately do not reveal names. Keep the original capture private and use its index to look up the actual request locally.

dsh-har-triage README · Install in Harness：Node 24.9+ is required. Install the prebuilt bundle into your chosen profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile YOUR_PROFILE add https://github.com/po-et/dsh-har-triage/releases/download/v0.1.2/dsh-har-triage-0.1.2.tgz
dsh --profile YOUR_PROFILE --dump-config
```

dsh-har-triage README · Install in Harness：Version 0.1.2 adds explicitly tested compatibility with Harness `0.2.1-rc.4` and `0.2.2-alpha.2`, verified on October 28, 2026, while retaining `0.2.1-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.3`. Older `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-alpha.2` peers remain accepted based on the original release's tests; they are not part of the current CI matrix.

dsh-har-triage README · Install in Harness：The configuration should contain the `har-triage` row. A configuration dump alone does not establish runtime compatibility. Start that profile, put your HAR inside its session workspace, and ask:

> Inspect capture.har with har_triage. Save reports in a new har-review directory. Explain the measured evidence and cite the original HAR entry indexes. Do not guess root causes.

Tool arguments:

```json
{"input":"capture.har","outputDir":"har-review","slowMs":2000}
```

dsh-har-triage README · Install in Harness：The tool uses Harness filesystem and sandbox services. It requires write permission to create the reports and refuses input/output paths outside the session workspace. Existing report files are never overwritten. Uninstall with `dsh plugin --profile YOUR_PROFILE remove dsh-har-triage`.

dsh-har-triage README · Try without Harness：The CLI and analysis/report modules use Node built-ins only. From a source checkout:

```sh
node src/cli.js capture.har --out new-report-directory --slow-ms 2000
```

Open `new-report-directory/report.html`. The output directory must not exist. The original capture is unchanged.

For a reproducible synthetic example:

```sh
npm run demo
```

dsh-har-triage README · Try without Harness：This creates a new directory under `artifacts/` with a deliberately synthetic capture and its report. It is not evidence of real browser traffic or real users.

dsh-har-triage README · Evidence, not root-cause claims：`503` means the capture records a server-error response. `status: 0` means it did not record a valid HTTP response. Neither identifies a failing service, proves CORS, or proves an expired token. A high wait/TTFB share is an observation, not proof that the backend or database is slow.

Start offsets include submillisecond differences and are expressed in relative milliseconds. Absolute source timestamps are never included in the report.

dsh-har-triage README · Evidence, not root-cause claims：Unknown phase timings and byte sizes remain `-1`, displayed as “Unknown.” TLS is part of the HAR connection timing and is not added a second time. Contradictory phase durations are flagged; the report hides misleading proportions.

Ollama's [`application/x-ndjson` streaming responses](https://docs.ollama.com/api/streaming) are classified as JSON. This is a MIME-based content category, not validation of the response body; model output remains excluded from reports.

dsh-har-triage README · What is retained and removed：Retained: source entry index, sequential endpoint alias, controlled method/status/content classes, relative offsets, numeric durations/sizes, and fixed diagnostic codes. Aliases group the same method/origin/path within one capture; query strings and fragments do not affect grouping.

dsh-har-triage README · What is retained and removed：HTTP method identity is case-sensitive: `GET` and `get` receive separate aliases. Only the allowlisted uppercase methods receive named display values; all other method tokens appear as `OTHER`. Private method tokens are used only for grouping and are not included in reports, tool evidence or report ID hashes.

dsh-har-triage README · What is retained and removed：Removed: complete URLs including origins and paths, query values, headers, cookies, request/response bodies, page titles, initiator data, IP addresses, absolute timestamps, extension fields, raw error text, and the original file digest. The report ID hashes only the retained projection. Arbitrary source strings are not copied to reports or tool evidence.

dsh-har-triage README · What is retained and removed：This is a minimal diagnostic projection, **not** a scrubbed HAR, an anonymization guarantee, or a replacement for reviewing an artifact before sharing it. Status patterns, sizes, timing, request counts and grouping can still identify an application. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

dsh-har-triage README · Limits：- HAR JSON only: version `1.2`, UTF-8, at most 16 MiB and 10,000 entries. Invalid supported entries fail with fixed errors rather than silently truncating the evidence.
- HTTP and HTTPS requests are analyzed. Other protocols are excluded and counted. Missing timing/size values are retained as unknown; a valid request URL, start timestamp, duration, status and response content object are required.
- Synchronous bounded analysis: cancellation is checked before parsing and between entries, not an interruptible worker. The slow threshold defaults to 2,000 ms and is configurable per call.
- Reports are created exclusively. If HTML creation fails after JSON creation, the JSON is retained and the tool reports the partial result; retry using a fresh destination.
- No upload, traffic replay, header inspection, body analysis, automatic source lookup, or edits to the original HAR.

dsh-har-triage README · Development and validation：```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run smoke:host
npm run smoke:profile -- /absolute/path/to/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh

dsh-har-triage README · Development and validation：The 60 tests cover actual CLI subprocesses, controlled output and failure text, input limits, phases, original-file preservation, and real Cordis tool dispatch/filesystem/sandbox/Loader integration. CI runs them on Node 24 and 26. `smoke:host` uses a real service composition; `smoke:profile` requires pnpm on PATH, packs this checkout, installs its tarball with the specified Harness CLI into a fresh temporary Profile, boots it with `runProfile`, and dispatches `har_triage`. Test files and Profiles are retained under the OS temporary directory for inspection.

dsh-har-triage README · Development and validation：The packed bundle was installed and exercised on Harness `0.2.1-rc.4` and `0.2.2-alpha.2`, in addition to the prior rc.2/rc.3 acceptance. The alpha host uses its new batch tool-execution API; the plugin itself is unchanged. Source bytes were unchanged; output omitted the synthetic canary; overwrite and workspace-escape attempts were refused. HMR is disabled only in the temporary Profiles. CI and the release workflow repeat these checks on all four versions. No LLM or real credentials are used. These synthetic checks establish the tested runtime behavior; they are not evidence of real-user usefulness.

dsh-har-triage README · Development and validation：Browser checks covered status filtering, signal-to-request navigation, correct source locators, no console errors, and a 390-pixel layout without page-level overflow. The demo and regression captures are synthetic; real-user usefulness is not yet validated.

dsh-har-triage README · Related tools：[net-debug](https://github.com/JohnXu22786/net-debug) is an existing Harness HTTP client with history, replay and HAR export. [harlite](https://github.com/brucehart/harlite) already offers extensive HAR analysis, SQL, waterfall and HTML reporting. This plugin does not replace those tools: its narrower purpose is a Harness-native, no-external-binary, allowlisted evidence path for agent-assisted debugging.
